title: [English Subtitles] Let's take a look at how racing suits are made using CLO~ The collaboration story between PRISMA and CLO
description: Let's take a look at how racing suits are made using CLO~ The collaboration story between PRISMA and CLO
transcript:
Dainese is a company that primarily works on and produces technical equipment for motorcyclists, and not only that, but also technical equipment for skiing, cycling, and outfitting.  
Before the introduction of 3D, I mainly used Adobe Illustrator and developed the entire process, the whole workflow at a creative level, always with Adobe Illustrator.  
After that, I spent my time with Adobe Illustrator.  
I created sketches for the product technicians and modelers, and from there the entire product development process began, the creation of model cards, the creation of the first prototype, corrections, and the whole workflow.  
We mainly adopted a 3D solution within the workflow, primarily to, one, quickly interpret the ideas from the style office, to present the project developments clearly and usefully to everyone, to reduce the number of prototypes, also for sustainability reasons, and also to reduce the time required for prototype definition.  
How did you start with 3D?  
From the moment we introduced 3D into the workflow, we really found many advantages, especially a reduction in time for prototype definition, because, let’s say, from the moment I develop the sketch with 3D, or in any case develop the project with 3D, the advantage is that the product technicians and modelers already have the model cards made.  
I’m not saying that it replaces their work, but it’s a big advantage for them; it’s also a big advantage on my part to already have the product with all the proportions in place.  
What is the big difference between 3D and 2D?  
In terms of prototypes, let’s say that the big difference with 3D is that, not always, but in 90% of cases, we arrive at the final product with the first prototype, whereas before, working with Adobe Illustrator and two-dimensional designs, we needed a few more prototypes, sometimes two, three, if not four prototypes.  
What is the difference between 3D and 2D?  
Let’s say that 3D has been a great help for all parts of the company, not only the style department, because with 3D, you actually already see an almost realistic product even before it comes out, so even people who are not used to seeing, let’s say, two-dimensional sketches, when they see them in three dimensions, it has an entirely different feel, let’s call it that.  
Even at a decision-making level, we manage to have some decisions anticipated compared to two-dimensional work.  
I repeat, it has all been to our advantage.  
What solutions have you seen compared to Claw?  
We had seen other solutions compared to Claw, but at a visual level, and also in terms of ease of use, we chose Claw precisely for the reasons I just mentioned.  
Because we say that Claw is not an excessively technical program and it is possible to use it even without having solid models.  
And so we chose it precisely for this reason and to implement it first of all in the creative part, and not only, because currently in the company, not only designers have Claw, but also some modelers.  
What are your plans for the future?  
We intend to implement more 3D in the future, not only in our area, but also as support, or in any case to develop it to assist marketing, such as in e-commerce.  
What are your plans for the future?  
We hope this 3D platform will be useful to enable this new technology and further advance our business and our business perspective.  
Can you suggest a solution for the future?  
We are trying to find a way to support our customers through a more specific and collaborative approach.  
How to get in contact with Claw in person?  
We will write you feedback about Claw’s product or sales; this is our first step, and we will try to ask you if you have any questions.  
In the future, in the future,

chunks.content: ## Overview of Dainese and Their Design Workflow Evolution This section introduces Dainese, a company specializing in technical equipment for motorcyclists, skiing, and cycling, and outlines their transition from traditional 2D design processes using Adobe Illustrator to incorporating 3D technology in product development. Key terms include 3D workflow, Adobe Illustrator, product technicians, modelers, and prototype development. Dainese primarily produces technical apparel and protective gear for motorcyclists, as well as equipment for skiing and cycling. Initially, their design process relied heavily on Adobe Illustrator, where sketches were created by designers and then passed to product technicians and modelers. This workflow included developing model cards, creating initial prototypes, and making necessary corrections. The shift toward integrating 3D solutions aimed to improve several aspects of the design process: faster interpretation of ideas from the style office, clearer project presentations, reduction in the number of physical prototypes (enhancing sustainability), and decreased time for prototype finalization. --- ## Advantages of Incorporating 3D Technology in Product Development This section explains the benefits Dainese experienced by adopting 3D design workflows, especially in prototype accuracy, time savings, and cross-departmental collaboration. Important concepts include prototype reduction, model cards, realistic visualization, and decision-making acceleration. Upon introducing 3D into their workflow, Dainese observed significant advantages, primarily a reduction in the time needed to finalize prototypes. When designs are developed in 3D, product technicians and modelers receive complete model cards early, streamlining their work without replacing their expertise. A major difference between 3D and 2D workflows is the prototype accuracy: about 90% of the time, the first physical prototype matches the final product when using 3D, compared to multiple iterations (two to four prototypes) previously required with 2D sketches. 3D visualization also benefits non-technical stakeholders by presenting nearly realistic representations of products early in the process, improving understanding and facilitating earlier decision-making compared to traditional 2D sketches. --- ## Choosing CLO for 3D Design: Criteria and Implementation This section describes why Dainese selected CLO as their preferred 3D software solution, highlighting ease of use, visual quality, and its applicability for both designers and modelers. It also touches on comparisons with other software and initial deployment strategies. Keywords include CLO, 3D software, usability, visual fidelity, and modelers. While evaluating alternatives to CLO, Dainese prioritized a solution that balanced visual quality with usability. CLO was chosen because it is not overly technical, allowing users without deep expertise in solid modeling to effectively operate the software. The initial focus was to implement CLO primarily within the creative design phase. Presently, both designers and some modelers in the company use CLO, indicating its integration beyond just the style department. --- ## Future Plans for 3D Integration and Business Development This section outlines Dainese’s strategic intentions to expand the use of 3D technology beyond design, including marketing and e-commerce support, and to foster deeper collaboration with customers. Key phrases include 3D platform expansion, marketing support, e-commerce, collaborative customer approach, and business advancement.

Key phrases include 3D platform expansion, marketing support, e-commerce, collaborative customer approach, and business advancement. Dainese plans to further develop their 3D capabilities not only within the design and production areas but also to support marketing activities such as e-commerce visualization. They anticipate that the 3D platform will drive new technological adoption and help advance their overall business perspective. Additionally, the company seeks to enhance customer support through more specific and collaborative approaches, possibly leveraging 3D solutions to improve communication and product customization. --- ## Communication and Feedback Regarding CLO This brief section notes Dainese’s intent to provide feedback to CLO’s sales and product teams, indicating a willingness to engage in direct communication to optimize their use of the software. Dainese plans to share their experience and feedback about CLO’s products and services as an initial step in building a collaborative relationship. They are open to further inquiries and discussions to refine their use of the technology.
